messages:
maria: quick question — if a client connection to frontdoor aborts midstream but upstream keeps producing, who owns retries / resumability? thinking about billing and side effects.

aj: short answer: need a single owner. leaning edge=fastfail for non-idempotent, but resume-token for streaming could be edge-managed.

sam: edge-managed resume token makes sense only if we persist minimal state. otherwise we push to upstream to handle resume semantics.

kai: i worry about memory/scale if edge holds open resume windows per client. what if a customer opens 10k streams then disconnects?

lina: proposal: edge issues ephemeral resume tokens with embedded routing hints + short TTL (e.g., 60s). token can be presented to any gateway to pick up with idempotency guard upstream.

maria: +1. also need clear env var to opt into long-tail resume for dedicated/private customers.

aj: concrete policy sketch:

```yaml
resume_policy:
  mode: edge-ephemeral
  ttl_seconds: 60
  bind_to_backend: false
  accept_from_any_frontdoor: true
```

sam: what about side effects? if upstream executed a mutation then retry could double-run.

lina: require ops to surface an idempotency-key for side-effecting calls. if absent, default policy = fail fast (no resume).

kai: operational note: telemetry + billing must attribute tokens to session origin for usage chargebacks. we need trace cookie in token.

maria: I'll draft an RFC addendum: edge issues token + trace, upstream validates token and dedupes using idempotency-key if present. If upstream can't dedupe, it can return 409 and edge will surface error to client.

ops-bot: created rfc draft: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/edge-resume-token-2026 (draft) :white_check_mark:

aj: next steps — maria to own draft, sam + kai to review perf/ops implications, lina to write small integration test for idempotency header handling. target: end of sprint.

maria: assigning myself, will post PR link soon. thanks all :rocket:
